We will be conducting packet analysis with ready-to-use tools that are implemented in Wireshark. 

**Statistics** 

- There are multiple statistics options that can be used for deeper investigation and allow users to see the bigger picture.  
- In the Statistics tab, there are many options that can be utilized; we will only cover the main ones that are most useful when identifying threats.  

**Resolved Addresses** 
- This helps analyst identify IP addresses and DNS available in the captured file.  
- This provides a list of the IP addresses and the host names of the IP addresses. 

![](data:image/png;base64,) ![](data:image/png;base64,) 

**Protocol Hierarchy** 
- Assist analyst by breaking down all available protocols from the capture file in a tree view based on packets, counters and percentages. 
    

![](data:image/png;base64,) 

![](data:image/png;base64,) 

**Conversations** 
- This represents traffic between two specific endpoints. This provides conversations in formats of ethernet, IPv4, IPv6, TCP, and UDP. 
    

![](data:image/png;base64,) 

**Endpoints** 
- This is similar to conversations; however, this provides unique information for a single information field. 
    

![](data:image/png;base64,) 

- Can also display the name of the Address as well.  
    

![](data:image/png;base64,) 

- Can also provide a Geo-location of the IP address as well. 
    

![](data:image/png;base64,)

**Statistics | Protocol Details**  
**IPv4 and IPv6** 
-  **IPv4 (123.456.7.8)** – is a 32bit address space that provides 4.3 billion unique addresses that is divided into 3 parts of the IPv4.  
	I. Network: identifies the network 
	II. Host: Identifies the machine on the network 
	III. Subnet Number: optional part of the IPv4 to divide large network into  smaller sub-networks.  
- **IPv6 (2001:0db8:0000:0000:0000:8a2e:0370:7334) or (2001:db8::8a2e:370:7334) omitting zeros** – is a 128-bit address that simplifies the headers address to reduce the process by routers.  
- **Support SLAAC (Stateless Address Autoconfiguration Configuration)** -  allows devices to configure their own IP address automatically without the  need of a **DHCP (Domain Host Configuration Protocol)** - Automate the  process of configuring devices on IP networks. It allows devices to receive IP  addresses and other network configurations dynamically.

- This section only focuses on packets that contain specific IP addresses. 
- This assist analyst to identify and list all events linked to a specific IP version. 
    

![](data:image/png;base64,)

**Protocol Filters**  
- Wireshark supports 3000 protocols and allows packet-level investigation by filtering protocols. 

**IP Filtering** 
- Help analyst filter the traffic according to the IP information from the packets (Network layer of the OSI model). 

|                          |                                                                                                                                                         |
| ------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Filter                   | Description                                                                                                                                             |
| ip                       | Show all IP packets.                                                                                                                                    |
| ip.addr == 10.10.10.111  | Show all packets containing IP address 10.10.10.111.                                                                                                    |
| ip.addr == 10.10.10.0/24 | Show all packets containing IP addresses from 10.10.10.0/24 subnet.                                                                                     |
| ip.src == 10.10.10.111   | Show all packets originated from 10.10.10.111                                                                                                           |
| ip.dst == 10.10.10.111   | Show all packets sent to 10.10.10.111                                                                                                                   |
| ip.addr vs ip.src/ip.dst | Note: The ip.addr filters the traffic without considering the packet direction. The ip.src/ip.dst filters the packet depending on the packet direction. |

**Transport Layer 4 TCP and UDP Filters**  
- Helps analyst filter the traffic according to protocol-level information from the packet (Transport layer of the OSI model).  
    
|   |   |   |   |
|---|---|---|---|
|Filter|Description|Filter|Expression|
|tcp.port == 80|Show all TCP packets with port 80|udp.port == 53|Show all UDP packets with port 53|
|tcp.srcport == 1234|Show all TCP packets originating from port 1234|udp.srcport == 1234|Show all UDP packets originating from port 1234|
|tcp.dstport == 80|Show all TCP packets sent to port 80|udp.dstport == 5353|Show all UDP packets sent to port 5353|

**Application-Level Protocol Filters | HTTP and DNS**  
- Help analyst filters the traffic according to application protocol level information from the packets (Application layer of the OSI model).  

|                               |                                                |                         |                          |
| ----------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------- | ----------------------- | ------------------------ |
| Filter                        | Description                                    | Filter                  | Description              |
| http                          | Show all HTTP packets                          | dns                     | Show all DNS packets     |
| http.response.code == 200     | Show all packets with HTTP response code "200" | dns.flags.response == 0 | Show all DNS requests    |
| http.request.method == "GET"  | Show all HTTP GET requests                     | dns.flags.response == 1 | Show all DNS responses   |
| http.request.method == "POST" | Show all HTTP POST requests                    | dns.qry.type == 1       | Show all DNS "A" records |


**Display Filter Expressions** 
- Stores all supported protocol structures to help analysts create display filters.  
- Provides an easy-to-use display filter builder guide. 

1. **What is the number of IP packets?**  
- To find the number of packets, we can input “ip” in the display filter. 
    

![](data:image/png;base64,) 

Answer 81,420 

2. **What is the number of packets with a “TTL value less than 10”?** 
- To determine the number of packets with the TTL (Time-To-Live) less than 10, we will have to put in a filter that will inform Wireshark to do such a task.  
- The filter we will input will be ip.ttl<10  
- The filter tells Wireshark to only look for packets that are less than 10 secs to live. 
    

![](data:image/png;base64,) 

Answer: 66 

3. **What is the number of packets which use “TCP port 4444”?** 
- In order for us to generate packets with only tcp port number 4444, we will input:  
- *tcp.port == 4444*   
    

![](data:image/png;base64,) 

Answer: 632 

4. **What is the number of “HTTP GET” request sent to port “80”**  
- For this to generate correctly, we will have to ask Wireshark for two filter requests at the same time. 
- *http.get.request.method == GET* <--- this tells Wireshark to generate packet with the HTTP GET request  
- *tcp.port == 80* <--- this informs Wireshark to find packets with port 80  
- *http.request.method == GET && tcp.port == 80* <--- we are now informing Wireshark to generate packets that have GET request and is targeting port 80.  
    

![](data:image/png;base64,)Answer: 527 

5. **What is the number of type A DNS Queries?** 
- To generate these results, we will need to generate 2 requests in the display filter.  
- *dns.flags.response == 1* <--- this tells Wireshark to only look for DNS that have a flag response that the bit is set to “1”.  
- *dns.qry.type == 1* <--- this tells Wireshark to look for dns query that are type (A) Address records referring to the “Queries” of the DNS packets  
- To join both filters together the input would be: 
-  *dns.flags.response == 1 && dns.qry.type == 1* 
    

![](data:image/png;base64,)Answer: 51 

**Advance Filtering**  

- In this write up we will focus on the specific packet details for the event of interest.  

**Filter: "contains"** 

|   |   |
|---|---|
|Filter|contains|
|Type|Comparison Operator|
|Description|Search for value inside packets. It is case-sensitive and provides similar functionality to the "Find" option by focusing on a specific field.|
|Example|Find all "Apache" servers.|
|Workflow|List all HTTP packets where packets' "server" field contains the "Apache" keyword.|
|Usage|http.server contains "Apache"|

![](data:image/png;base64,) 

**Filter: "matches"** 

|   |   |
|---|---|
|Filter|matches|
|Type|Comparison Operator|
|Description|Search a pattern of a regular expression. It is case insensitive, and complex queries have a margin of error.|
|Example|Find all .php and .html pages.|
|Workflow|List all  HTTP packets where packets' "host" fields match keywords ".php" or ".html".|
|Usage|http.host matches "\.(php\|html)"|

![](data:image/png;base64,) 

**Filter: "in"** 

|   |   |
|---|---|
|Filter|in|
|Type|Set Membership|
|Description|Search a value or field inside of a specific scope/range.|
|Example|Find all packets that use ports 80, 443 or 8080.|
|Workflow|List all TCP packets where packets' "port" fields have values 80, 443 or 8080.|
|Usage|tcp.port in {80 443 8080}|

![](data:image/png;base64,) 

**Filter: "upper"** 

|   |   |
|---|---|
|Filter|upper|
|Type|Function|
|Description|Convert a string value to uppercase.|
|Example|Find all "APACHE" servers.|
|Workflow|Convert all  HTTP packets' "server" fields to uppercase and list packets that contain the "APACHE" keyword.|
|Usage|upper(http.server) contains "APACHE"|

![](data:image/png;base64,) 

**Filter: "lower"** 

|   |   |
|---|---|
|Filter|lower|
|Type|Function|
|Description|Convert a string value to lowercase.|
|Example|Find all "apache" servers.|
|Workflow|Convert all  HTTP packets' "server" fields info to lowercase and list packets that contain the "apache" keyword.|
|Usage|lower(http.server) contains "apache"|

![](data:image/png;base64,) 

**Filter: "string"** 

|   |   |
|---|---|
|Filter|string|
|Type|Function|
|Description|Convert a non-string value to a string.|
|Example|Find all frames with odd numbers.|
|Workflow|Convert all "frame number" fields to string values, and list frames end with odd values.|
|Usage|string(frame.number) matches "[13579]$"|

![](data:image/png;base64,) 

**Bookmarks** 

- Wireshark allows filters to be saved as bookmarks and buttons for later usage.  
    

![](data:image/png;base64,) 

1. **Find all Microsoft IIS servers. What is the number of packets that did not originate from “port 80”?** 
- To determine the number of packets that did not originate from port 80, we will have to execute a combined filter.  
- *http.server contains “IIS”* <--- this filter is telling Wireshark to ONLY look for servers that  “contains” IIS 
- *tcp.srcport != 80* <--- this is asking Wireshark to alleviate port 80 within the search 
- Joined together as a filter it will be  
*http.server contains “IIS” && tcp.srcport != 80* 

![](data:image/png;base64,)Answer: 21 

2. **Find all Microsoft IIS Servers. What is the number of packets that have “version 7.5”?** 
- This will be another joined filter  
- Similar to the first filter in question 1 it will be http.server contains “IIS” 
- Then the next filter will be *http.server matches “7.5”* <--- this telling Wireshark to only find matches of 7.5 version of the server IIS  
- Together you will have *http.server contains “IIS”* *&& http.server matches “7.5”* 
    

![](data:image/png;base64,)Answer: 71 

3. **What is the total number of packets that use port 3333,4444, or 9999?** 
- To generate the number of packets that have any of the specific ports above, we will filter is with *tcp.port in {333 444 999}* <---- this will let Wireshark know we only interested in the port within the braces  

![](data:image/png;base64,)Answer: 2235 

4. **What is the number of packets with “even TTL numbers”?** 
- In this filter we will be using a string to filter in TTL with only even numbers  
- The filter input would be *string(ip.ttl) matches "[02468]$"* 
- this is asking Wireshark to search for patterns within the character class “[02468]$” for the value of “ip.ttl”, which normally have integers between 0 and 255.  
- The “$” indicates that the filter ensure the even digit must be the last number of the TTL.  
    

![](data:image/png;base64,)Answer: 77289
